q: Which best describes the interdependence of the two stages of photosynthesis?
options: The Calvin cycle supplies O2 to the light reactions, which supply CO2 to the Calvin cycle
Light reactions supply ATP and NADPH; the Calvin cycle returns ADP, Pi and NADP+ to them
The two stages are independent, so the Calvin cycle can run indefinitely in darkness
The light reactions supply glucose to the Calvin cycle, which turns it into starch
explanation: ATP and NADPH from the thylakoids power the reduction of GP and the regeneration of RuBP. In turn, the Calvin cycle regenerates ADP + Pi (needed by ATP synthase) and NADP+ (the final electron acceptor of PSI). If either stage stops, the other soon stops too. The Calvin cycle is called 'light-independent' only because it doesn't use light directly.
